name: Philosophy (Min)

rules.name: History of Philosophy
rules.desc: Complete a History of Philosophy course numbered 100 or above and for a minimum of three units.

rules.name: Electives (PHIL courses numbered 10 and above)
rules.desc: Any course 10 and above except for 196-199.

grading:
No more than ten units with grades of Satisfactory (S) or Credit (CR) can be used to satisfy the minor requirements.
Any courses taken for a letter grade to fulfill requirements must be taken for a minimum of 3 units and completed with a grade of 'C-' or higher. No more than six units with grades of Satisfactory (S) or Credit (CR) can be used to satisfy the minor requirements. At least 10 units must be from courses numbered 100 or above. PHIL 196-199 do not count towards the unit requirement.
transferPolicy: A maximum of two transfer courses for a combined maximum of 10 units can be used for the minor. In general, transfer courses cannot be substituted for required courses.
reviewNotes: The audit checks two of the three contemporary areas (philosophy of science or logic, moral and political philosophy, contemporary theoretical philosophy) and Philosophy electives numbered 10 and above to reach 30 units, at least 10 of them numbered 100 or above. PHIL 196-199 do not count, letter-graded courses need a C- or better, and at most 10 units graded S or CR count. Checked by hand: a history of philosophy course numbered 100 or above, which you move in, the 3-unit minimum for letter-graded courses, and at most two transfer courses for 10 units. The Bulletin gives the S/CR limit as both ten and six units, so confirm it with the department.

totals.label: S or CR units (at most 10 count)
